query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Developing a new, more accurate interatomic potential using a machine learning approach, specifically a neural network potential (NNP) with a graph neural network (GNN) architecture, trained on a dataset of ab initio molecular dynamics simulations of multicomponent high-entropy alloys, can improve the representation of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid of multicomponent high-entropy alloys, thereby reducing the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references.
generation.material_initial_state: Solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures
generation.intervention: Development and application of a new neural network potential (NNP) for multicomponent high-entropy alloys, using a graph neural network (GNN) architecture, trained on a dataset of ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, with optimization methods including mean squared error minimization and Bayesian optimization
generation.conditions: High melting temperatures, composition ranges of 3-6 principal elements (defined as elements with concentrations greater than 5 at.%) with concentrations between 10-30 at.%, and temperature ranges of 0.8-1.2 T_m, where T_m is the melting temperature
generation.structural_mediator: Short-range order (SRO), defined as the arrangement of atoms within the first coordination shell, and medium-range order (MRO), defined as the arrangement of atoms within the second and third coordination shells, in the liquid state, measured using pair correlation functions and cluster analysis
generation.mechanism: Improved capture of complex many-body interactions and atomic configurations by the NNP, through the use of a GNN architecture that can learn hierarchical representations of atomic environments, leading to enhanced reference-target phase-space overlap, and reduced thermodynamic-integration path mismatch, due to the ability of the NNP to accurately predict the free energy landscape of the system
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 25% relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, as measured by the difference in free energy curves, in units of meV/atom
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 0.8-1.2 T_m, where T_m is the melting temperature; composition range: 3-6 principal elements with concentrations between 10-30 at.%
generation.uncertainty: The accuracy of the NNP may be limited by the quality of the training data, and the transferability of the NNP to different composition and temperature ranges may be affected by the choice of architecture and optimization methods

falsification_experiment.design: Molecular dynamics simulations using the new NNP and TOR-TILD’s EAM references, with calculations of free energy curves and comparison of thermodynamic-integration path mismatch, and a control experiment using TOR-TILD’s EAM references as a baseline for comparison
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch is less than 20% relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, or if the difference in free energy curves is greater than 10 meV/atom, the hypothesis is falsified
